correctness.rationale: The point-process convergence follows from iid endpoint-corner rare-cell Poisson limits; the exact conditional binomial degree law, a deterministic localization bound and Chernoff estimates exclude noncorner low degrees; uniform concentration maps each corner to degree 2v. A disjoint third corner and an almost surely continuous random-rectangle map give the joint universal process. The intensity transform, conditional Poisson mechanism and explicit Rayleigh moment and polar-angle integration prove the positive exact limiting covariance and all corollaries. The verifier passed 11,491 finite checks; these are cross-checks rather than proofs.

value.rationale: The lowest-degree vertices are a natural robustness statistic in random interval networks, previously controlled only through their minimum. All low-degree multiplicities, side localization, endpoint shape, and order statistics follow from the new entire Poisson spectrum. The already-known universal-vertex process is linked nontrivially through shared boundary minima, revealing positive dependence between opposite degree extremes with an exact covariance constant and an exact conditional Poisson rate. This connection is not obtainable from the marginal known results.
